figure4A.source: RESOLVED at cycle 87. Figure 4's legend cites refs 12 and 30 for (AAQAA)n. Ref 30 IS NEVER PRINTED - the reference list ends at 29, confirmed at 300 dpi on p.509 - so it cannot be chased, and cycle 63's 'lost in typesetting' reading stands. Ref 12 (Munoz & Serrano 1994, Nat. Struct. Biol. 1, 399-409) does not carry the series, as cycle 68 established. THE SOURCE IS MUNOZ & SERRANO 1995-II, J. Mol. Biol. 245, 275-296 - refs 13/14 of the same list, under doc/ with a clean text layer, and not checked in cycles 63-68. Its Results: 'In Figure 2 we show the length-dependence of the helical content for different N and C-terminal blocked polyalanine-based peptides; (AAKAA)n (Rohl et al., 1992), (AEAAKA)n (Scholtz et al., 1991c) and (AAQAA)n (ANALYSED HERE with the exception of the 16-residue peptide, which has been analysed by Scholtz et al., 1991b).'
figure4A.status: 0 C / 0.1 M retained. Corroborated for one point, inferred for three.

previous_coded_value.note: WRONG for the three points Munoz measured himself. Superseded at cycle 87.

figure4A.conditions_quote: Munoz & Serrano 1995-II, Materials and Methods: 'Jasco-710 instrument at a temperature of 5 C. The peptides (roughly 1.5 mg) were dissolved in 1 ml of 2.5 mM sodium phosphate buffer (pH 7.0), unless otherwise indicated.' / Figure 1 legend: 'The spectra were acquired at 5 C, in 2.5 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.0), peptide concentration was 25 microM.'
figure4A.ionic_strength_derivation: DERIVED. 2.5 mM sodium phosphate at pH 7.0: the H2PO4-/HPO4(2-) speciation at pKa2 = 7.20 gives I = 0.00443 M by I = 0.5*sum(c*z^2) with Na+ set by electroneutrality. Coded 0.0044. NOT the 0.1 M previously carried, which was an inference with no source behind it.
figure4A.mixed_conditions_warning: THIS PANEL DOES NOT SHARE ONE SET OF CONDITIONS. Three of the four points (n = 1, 2, 4) are Munoz's own, at 5 C / I = 0.0044 M. The 16-residue point is Scholtz et al. 1991b (JACS 113, 5102), measured at 0 C in 0.1 M NaCl / 1 mM phosphate, I = 0.102 M. The harness resolves conditions per PANEL, not per point, so the panel is coded at Munoz's conditions - right for 3 of 4 rather than the previous 1 of 4. The 16-mer is the residual known defect in this panel's conditions.
figure4A.y_values_open: NOT CHANGED, and this is the open part of the finding. The plotted values 0.33 / 16.62 / 41.14 / 56.79 are Munoz's 1997 REPLOT. N050's cycle-65 normalisation hypothesis is NOT overturned and now has a second anchor: Scholtz's own scale gives 49.84% for the 16-mer and a flat theta_H of -40,000 gives 42.18%, against the 41.14 plotted; and 1995-II Figure 2's own bar for the same peptide reads about 49 by eye. So 1997 Figure 4A appears renormalised against BOTH. The clean next operation is to re-digitise 1995-II Figure 2's (AAQAA)n bars, which are primary and carry stated conditions, and replace this digitisation of a replot entirely.
figure4A.effect_measured: Cycle 87, like-for-like on the three points the model can evaluate (the 5-residue member is below pyagadir's six-residue minimum and now scores in nothing). Panel RMSE 10.742 -> 8.705 from the abscissa, sequence and conditions correction alone; all three points moved toward the measurement. THE TWO DEFECTS CORROBORATE EACH OTHER: applying N050's cycle-65 normalisation on top of the corrected abscissa - y_true = y_plotted * 40000/(40000*(1-2.5/n)) - gives 22.16/48.76/64.90 against pyagadir's 18.81/48.07/70.00, RMSE 3.544, and the residuals change sign (+3.35/+0.69/-5.10) instead of being uniformly one-signed. Cycle 65 left the hypothesis unapplied because only one of four points had a primary source; three of four now do. NOT APPLIED HERE either - the definitive test is re-digitising 1995-II Figure 2's (AAQAA)n bars, not arithmetic on a replot. Reproduce: reasoning/evidence/scripts/run_benchmarks.py.

figure4B.source: VERIFIED. Figure 4's legend: "(B) (AAKAA)n.21 The experimental average helical contents of this set of peptides have been derived from the fractional occupancies of the amide protons measured by Rohl et al.21 using their equation 5." Ref 21 = Rohl, C.A., Scholtz, J.M., York, E.J., Stewart, J.M. & Baldwin, R.L. (1992) 'Kinetics of Amide Proton Exchange in Helical Peptides of Varying Chain Lengths', Biochemistry 31, 1263-1269 -- under doc/, and confirmed by its generic formula Ac-(AAKAA)nY-NH2 and chain lengths 6-51. The data are the NMR H/D-exchange experiment, NOT the CD experiment. Its conditions: "At t = 0 min, the peptide was dissolved at 1-2 mM in 2H2O at 5 C containing 1 M NaCl and 5 mM sodium phosphate, pH* 2.50." Confirmed downstream: "The average helix-coil constants determined for the peptides at 5 C are w = 1.58 and u2 = 0.0023."
figure4B.ionic_strength_derivation: 1 M NaCl + 5 mM sodium phosphate; I = 1.005 M, coded 1.0. Not a derivation of the Lacroix kind -- the salt dominates by 200x and the buffer is negligible.
figure4B.pH_note: pH* 2.50 is the glass-electrode reading in 2H2O uncorrected for the isotope effect (the paper says so); true pD ~ 2.9. Coded 2.5. IMMATERIAL for this peptide by construction: Ac/NH2 caps leave only Lys (pKa ~10.5) and Tyr (pKa ~10) ionisable, and both are in the same state at pH 2.5 and at 7.0. Measured at cycle 60: changing pH alone 7.0 -> 2.5 moves this panel's predictions by <0.01 percentage points.

previous_coded_value.note: WRONG. Ionic strength was low by 10x and temperature by 5 C. Superseded at cycle 60; see reasoning/nodes/N046.md for the measured effect.

figure4C.source: VERIFIED. Figure 4's legend: "(C) (AEAAKA)n.20" Ref 20 = Scholtz, J.M., Qian, H., York, E.J., Stewart, J.M. & Baldwin, R.L. (1991) 'Parameters of Helix-Coil Transition Theory for Alanine-Based Peptides of Varying Chain Lengths in Water', Biopolymers 31, 1463-1470 -- under doc/, and confirmed by its generic formula Ac-Y(AEAAKA)kF-NH2, which matches this panel's peptides exactly. Its CD Measurements section: "CD samples were prepared by diluting aqueous stock solutions of peptide with either a buffer consisting of 1 mM sodium citrate, 1 mM sodium phosphate, 1 mM sodium borate, and 0.10 M sodium chloride, or with 1 mM potassium phosphate containing 0.10 M potassium fluoride. In either case the pH was adjusted with HCl and KOH or NaOH to pH 7.0 at room temperature." Temperature: the paper reports thermal unfolding curves and quotes helix propagation as s(0 C); Figure 4C plots single helicities, taken as the 0 C end of those curves.
figure4C.ionic_strength_derivation: 0.10 M NaCl (or KF) + 3 mM buffer salts; I ~ 0.105 M, coded 0.1. Within 5%.
figure4C.status: 0 C / 0.1 M retained and now VERIFIED rather than inferred.
figure4C.abscissa_corrected: CORRECTED at cycle 64. The coded peptide lengths were 20, 26, 32, 50, 62 and are now 14, 20, 26, 32, 50 -- the same five helicity values shifted one peptide shorter. Two independent grounds. (1) A 62-residue peptide DOES NOT EXIST in the source: Scholtz 1991 Figure 1's legend reads "CD spectra of all six peptides recorded at 0 C. The spectra correspond to chain lengths of 50, 38, 32, 26, 20, and 14 residues". (2) Reading the 0 C intercepts off Scholtz's Figure 2 and converting with the paper's OWN equations (3) and (4) -- theta_H = -40000*(1 - x/n) + 100*T, theta_C = 640 - 45*T, x = 2.5 from its Table I -- gives 37.7 (n=14), 73.3 (20), 84.6 (26), 88.3 (32), 88.5 (38), 93.5 (50). Against Munoz's five plotted values the mean absolute deviation is 15.13 as coded and 1.84 shifted. Munoz plots five of the six peptides, omitting n=38, whose value is within 0.2 of n=32's.

figure4A.peptide_note: CORRECTED at cycle 87. Ac-(AAQAA)n-NH2 for n = 1, 2, 4 plus Scholtz's Ac-(AAQAA)3Y-NH2 at n = 3. Lengths 5, 10, 16, 20, read off the x-axis of Munoz & Serrano 1995-II Figure 2 at 340 dpi. The previous coding was AAQAAY / AAQAAAAQAAY / AAQAAAAQAAAAQAAY / AAQAAAAQAAAAQAAAAQAAY, i.e. (AAQAA)nY for n = 1..4, lengths 6, 11, 16, 21 - a uniform +1 from assuming every member carries the Tyr. It does not: 1995-II states 'The (AAQAA)n peptides were synthesised WITHOUT a Tyr residue (with the exception of that with 16 residues, Scholtz et al., 1991b)'. Only the 16-mer keeps it, which is why the third point alone was already right.

helicity_provenance.what_changed: figure4A.helicity was 0.33 / 16.62 / 41.14 / 56.79 and is now 0.65 / 22.04 / 48.62 / 64.76. The peptides, lengths, caps and conditions are untouched by THIS change - they were corrected separately at cycle 87 and are described in _provenance.per_panel.figure4A.
helicity_provenance.why: Munoz 1997 Figure 4A is a REPLOT of measurements made elsewhere, and the replot converted ellipticity to percent helix with a LENGTH-INDEPENDENT theta_H of -40,000 where the source used the chain-length-corrected -40,000*(1-2.5/n). That under-reports helicity, and more so the shorter the peptide, which is exactly the shape of the residual this panel had. The hypothesis is N050's, raised at cycle 65.
helicity_provenance.the_evidence_that_settled_it: Cycle 93. The owner supplied Scholtz, Qian, Robbins & Baldwin (1993) Biochemistry 32, 9668-9676. Its Table II gives fractional helicities for the AQ peptide, Ac-AAQAAAAQAAAAQAAY-NH2 - which IS this panel's 16-residue point - and its footnote a states the scale outright: 'Fractional helicities were determined from the observed ellipticities ([theta]222) at 0 C ... using [theta]_H = -33 750 and [theta]_C = 640 deg cm2 dmol-1.' -33,750 is exactly -40,000*(1-2.5/16). The printed value is 0.49. Munoz plots 41.14; the renormalisation predicts 48.62. That is 0.38 points from a PRINTED PRIMARY NUMBER. Two further routes agree: Scholtz 1991 JACS gives 49.84 from its own -16,500 ellipticity, and Munoz & Serrano 1995-II Figure 2's own bar for the same peptide reads about 49 by eye. Four routes near 49 against a replot at 41.
helicity_provenance.the_transformation: y_true = y_plotted * (theta_H_flat - theta_C) / (theta_H(n) - theta_C) with theta_C = +640, theta_H_flat = -40,000 and theta_H(n) = -40,000*(1-2.5/n). Equivalently y_true = y_plotted * 40,640 / (40,000*(1-2.5/n) + 640). Factors applied: 1.9690 (n=5), 1.3264 (n=10), 1.1817 (n=16), 1.1403 (n=20). Rounded to 2 dp.
helicity_provenance.how_to_reverse: Multiply each value by the reciprocal of its factor, or simply restore `previous_values` below. Nothing else in this file depends on these numbers.
helicity_provenance.scope_and_limits: CONFIRMED for the 16-residue point against a printed primary number. The other three points are corrected by the same transformation on the strength of the MECHANISM being established, not because each has its own anchor - none of them does. The n=5 point is the weakest: theta_H(5) = -20,000 is a long extrapolation of a formula fitted on longer chains, and the factor 1.97 is the largest applied. It matters little in practice - Munoz 1995-II says the five-residue peptides' helical content is zero, both values round to under 1%, and pyagadir refuses the peptide anyway for being under six residues, so it scores in nothing.
helicity_provenance.could_be_wrong_if: Munoz did not in fact use a flat -40,000 but some other scale that happens to reproduce 41.14 at n=16. Nothing rules that out directly; what makes the flat -40,000 the right reading is that it is the SAME formula the source uses with the chain-length term dropped, which is a plausible slip, and that it reproduces the one point with a primary source to 0.38 points. If a future reading of Munoz 1995-II Figure 2's bars gives values materially different from 22.04 / 48.62 / 64.76 for n = 10, 16 and 20, this renormalisation is wrong and `previous_values` should be restored.
